title: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

sense.text:
Today’s topic is when the harvest is ripe. It’s a self-reflector: it’s related to the present day, but it’s all about getting our minds right, getting ourselves ready for when the harvest time does come.

“From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence.” We have to have an understanding of what Christ is speaking of here. That kingdom is the nation of Israel, and the kingdom of heaven suffers violence. So we got to ask the question why.

A lot of times we like to blame everything on the other nations, but think about it: if we was keepers at home, if we did what we were supposed to do, we wouldn’t be facing what we’re going through on the daily. We wouldn’t have to worry about the violence, the suffering, all of these things that come against us and what came against our forefathers as well. How did that come about? Sin. That’s how it came about.

precepts.why: Let’s find out who that kingdom of heaven is. “He hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” Over who? Over Israel. So the kingdom in Matthew 11 is referring to the nation of Israel, and it is that kingdom, Israel, that suffereth violence.

“For we suffer because of our sins.” If we would have did what we supposed to do, we wouldn’t have to worry about the violence and the suffering. That’s why the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence.

So let’s make sure we not throwing pity parties, getting down when trials and tribulations come against us. Getting fired, disagreements and things like that: those are little troubles. There’s a serious trouble that’s gonna come.

sense.text: “He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.” Who’s it speaking of? Jesus the Christ, the Messiah. Once again we read about him in the Old Testament and the Apocrypha. Christ was always there.

“Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall glory in the midst of her people. In the congregation of the most High shall she open her mouth”. Wisdom is Christ. “I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud”: Christ came out of the mouth of the Most High.
“I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.” He walked “in the bottom of the deep”. When you read Genesis 1, when you read Proverbs the 8th chapter, this is what it’s referring to.

“In the waves of the sea, and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I got a possession.” In every people, every nation, kindred and tongue, he has a possession. But watch this: “With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?” He came out of the mouth of the Most High, and he asks the question, in whose inheritance shall I abide.

“So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thine inheritance in Israel.”

We got to take a step back. The Creator of all things, the Most High God of the whole earth, created every nation, kindred and tongue, but he chose us, and he told his Son the same thing: wisdom dwells with us. But remember what we read earlier: the kingdom of heaven suffered violence. How did that come about? Sin.

precepts.why:
We’re going to put something together, going back and forth with Sirach 24. “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made”: this was in the beginning, when the Most High was preparing the world as we know it today, with all of the different land masses. “Even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.”

Sirach 24:9 gives the account that Christ was always there, created from the beginning before the world. This account shows the same beginning, and who the them is that the world was prepared for: us, Israel.

He came out of the mouth of the Most High and asked, in whose inheritance shall I abide? “O God of my father, and God of the inheritance of Israel”: the inheritance of who? Of Israel. He came out of the mouth of the Most High, so guess where he’s going to reside: the same place, Israel.

It goes on: “Lord of the heavens and earth, Creator of the waters, king of every creature”. The Creator of all things, who created everything, the earth, the moon, the stars, the waters, is the God of the inheritance of Israel. That is the Creator of all things that gave Christ the commandment in Sirach 24:8.

sense.text: “Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard.” Touching his vineyard, which is Israel, his inheritance. “My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill”.

“And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine”. He fenced it, meaning he took care of his vineyard. Think about the farmers when they have their crops, when they have inclement weather, all of the work they have to put in to keep that crop sustainable: that’s what he did for us. “And built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein”.

He nurtured us, he fed us, he clothed us. When you read Nehemiah 9, the shoes on our feet: we was walking for years and he didn’t even let that thing diminish. He provided manna from heaven, sweet water, all of that. So he’s like, okay, this should be fruitful because I cared for it, I nurtured it. “He looked that it should bring forth grapes”, meaning it should be fruitful.

“And it brought forth wild grapes”: not according to how he planned it or how he spoke it. We turned our back on God. We say we don’t appreciate your benefits, we don’t appreciate what you’ve done for us. We are covetous, we are hard-headed, we are stubborn, we want to go do it like the other nations, although he put his name in us.

precepts.why: Jump down to find out who the vineyard is: “For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel”. There it is.

He looked that his vineyard should bring forth grapes. “The wicked desireth the net of evil men: but the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit.” That’s how the Most High God intended us to be. He intended for the nation of Israel to be the representation of righteousness and holiness upon the earth.

We got to understand that, brothers and sisters, to get our minds right about the perilous times to come. In the midst of Jacob’s trouble we’re going to be catching hell on every side, but all of this is by design. We could have had it the easy way, but you know how Jake is: Jake don’t ever want to do nothing the easy way. Sometimes you gotta fail in order to see what you did was wrong, and the Most High knows that. He even prophesied our demise because he knew what was in us.

“And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy”. That’s how he intended us to be, fruitful, that great. “And have severed you from other people”: he separated us from the wicked, the other nations, and he put his laws and his name on us so we can exemplify that righteousness and that holiness.

sense.text: This goes along with the wild grapes: Israel was always stubborn when it comes to serving God. God gave us everything we need; we were that good vine, but we become degenerate. “They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them”: God gave us order to destroy the nations, and we did not destroy them.

“But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” Instead we mingle among them. We start following their ways, we start following their traditions, and you wonder why we in the bottom. That’s why.

“And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.” Their idols are a snare unto us, a trap. That’s why a lot of us try to figure it out and can’t figure out why: because we went against God’s word. That’s that snare. You trying to make it right, but you see yourself still going right back in the dip hole you’re in. You can never get right; you are that blind at noonday. You would think our grown men would be the wise ones to help the young ones, and they are worse than we are.

“Judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard. What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it?” He asks the question: I made you the greatest people on the face of the earth. When you asked for a king, I gave it to you. I clothed you. He gave us a land that’s very fruitful, natural resources. What else could the Most High God have done for our forefathers? Nothing else. And if he did, we would have still rebelled, and he knew that. “Wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes?”

“And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard”: because you want to rebel against me, now I’m going to show you what I’m going to do to you. “I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up”. The Most High has been our protection. Once he took that protection, that’s when our enemies was able to come in, and it’s a direct result of sin. Don’t forget that.

“And break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down”. He prophesied our demise multiple times. We gonna have to go through this in order to get back right with God. Lord’s will, this class could be some encouragement and upliftment for you as we continue to see the prophecies unfold, the dangers around us increase, the pestilence, the seditions.

“And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned”. Think about a vineyard, a crop: what’s gonna happen if you don’t water it, if you don’t shelter it from the cold? It’s going to be destroyed. What happened to us? We became destroyed as a people. He’s not gonna take care of his vineyard anymore: “nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.”

We had everything, all of those benefits from the Most High God, and he took them away, and over time we waxed worse and worse and worse.

precepts.why: What does it mean, I will take away the hedge? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence”. That’s the hedge being removed: he goes and returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence. That’s why the kingdom of heaven suffered violence. We have to understand that, brothers and sisters.

A basic precept for the vineyard laid waste and destroyed: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. There it is. When you forget the laws of God, you’re in the midst of sin.

sense.text: “The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field”. We understand what the kingdom of heaven is talking about. Think about what we read earlier in Sirach 24 and what this is tying into.
“But while men slept”: they was slumbering. “His enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.” When Israel wasn’t acting right, the enemy came in.

“But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.” The servants ask the householder what’s going on: “Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?” “He said unto them, An enemy hath done this.” “Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?”
“But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them.” If you do that, you’re gonna ruin the good fruit, the good harvest, the good crop.

“Let both grow together until the harvest”: because of this situation, let both of them grow together unto the harvest. “And in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them”, because that’s not the people. “But gather the wheat into my barn.” This is just surface level; we’re going to come back to this thought.

“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” When we were with the Most High in Christ, before we were sent to earth, we agreed; we were on one accord. We did not go against the commandment of God like we did when we got here.

“For then every one obeyed: but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”. When we got here to this world, our manners were corrupted by that perpetual seed. “And by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves”: they rid themselves of God’s laws. That’s what the forefathers did.

“So I considered the world, and, behold, there was peril because of the devices that were come into it.” Remember what we read in 2 Maccabees 7: we suffer because of sin. Peril means trouble, affliction, suffering. There was peril because of the devices that were come into the world: that was that corruptible seed.

“And I saw, and spared it greatly, and have kept me a grape of the cluster”. A grape of the cluster, because in the whole cluster it ain’t all right. Just like with the wheat, there’s some tares in that thing, there’s some wicked in that thing. “And a plant of a great people”: keep this in mind.
“Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”. So you mean to tell me God created people just to be destroyed? Absolutely, yes. God created people on this earth who ought to be destroyed.

precepts.why:
Let’s get an understanding of that perpetual seed that corrupted us when we got to this earth. “For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness hath it brought up unto this time?” Didn’t Adam have the kingdom? He had a kingdom, but he lost it through sin. Didn’t the nation of Israel have the kingdom? Israel had the same thing.

How much ungodliness has it brought up unto this time: our forefathers didn’t learn from Adam’s mistake; we kept that thing going. “And how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?” That time of threshing is the harvest. Evil is going to increase, a lot of evil; Isaiah said the earth is going to be turned into utter darkness. The evil is just going to keep going until the time of threshing comes.

Israel had the kingdom just like Adam: “That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” As the days of heaven upon earth. That goes back to Isaiah 5, when the Most High says what else could I have done for my vineyard. He gave us everything. We was in paradise on earth; we had it all, we had rulership, and we lost it through that same evil seed.

The multitude born in vain includes our own people. “Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel”. Just because you have Israelite blood flowing through your veins don’t make you an Israelite; that’s what the Bible is saying. We have a lot of wicked amongst our people: just look at your auntie, your mama, your uncles, your daddy, your brother, some of y’all that be coming here on the sabbath. Don’t get mad; it is what it is. That’s the wicked of our people that was born in vain.

sense.text:
We talked about the wicked of our people that was born in vain; now we got to touch the other people. “Hath not the potter power over the clay”: the potter is the creator, the clay is the creation. “Of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Absolutely, because he’s the creator, he could do whatever he wants to do. He can choose Israel and despise every other nation; that’s up to him.

Everybody got a problem with that, everybody has an issue with the fact that God chose Israel and none else. Take it up with the Most High. Don’t get mad at us; we just the messengers. The Most High God of heaven and earth happened to choose his inheritance to be in Israel.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. That’s what this class is about: the harvest is ripening. It’s not ripe yet, but we almost there. He endured with much longsuffering. Fitted to destruction means he made a creation to be destroyed. That’s what he did.

“And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”: the vessels of mercy are Israel, those who will receive mercy in the last days. He’ll have much longsuffering just to show all of his creation that at the end of the day, I choose who I want to choose; I’m the creator, I can do what I want to do. “Which he had afore prepared unto glory”. Y’all got to understand this thing: this was a fixed fight from the beginning.

precepts.why:
“Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker!” Whoever got a problem with how he was made is in direct opposition with the Most High God. China trying to be like America: there’s a big power struggle in the earth today because they see America on the decline. But they don’t want to give it to us willingly; they want to fight, and they think they got next. But God says we got next. Any of his creation that wants to strive against the creator, God says destruction is coming to you.

“Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth”, but don’t try to fight against God. That’s what they’re trying to do with the space station: they having sex in space, their wickedness. “Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou?” That’s what Esau does all day every day, because they believe that they are God on earth.

The vessels of mercy afore prepared unto glory. “According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”: he had chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, the same thing we read in Sirach 24:9 and 2 Esdras 9:18.

“That we should be holy”, because that’s how he made us: to be fruitful, to be that grape we read in Isaiah 5. Even though we became that wild grape, he said, I got a plan in place. I already knew you would fail, but now I’m gonna give you time for you to get yourself right. “And without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ”. He allowed us to go through all of this for us to receive Christ.

sense.text: “And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be”. That goes in with Isaiah 5:5, when he said he would remove the hedge, but he’s saying it right here in Deuteronomy, before we even had a king, before the Assyrians came, before Babylon came. “For they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” Who is that faith? Jesus the Christ. He knew we was a nation void of faith, so he said, you’re not ready for my Son yet. He had to put us through the trials, all of these things. He allowed it to happen. It was still our choice, but he knew what it was going to be.

“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people”. He’s already prophesying about the northern kingdom of Israel becoming gentiles: the split, before King Solomon was even on the earth.

precepts.why: Children in whom is no faith. “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. For by it the elders obtained a good report. Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God”. We read Sirach 24, Proverbs the 8th chapter, Genesis the first chapter: we understand who was doing that framing. Jesus the Christ.

“But without faith it is impossible to please him”. God knew that back in Deuteronomy. He knew we was a nation without faith, so we were not ready for his Son yet, and he had to put us through the trials first.

sense.text: By faith and suffering through Christ: that’s the same thing our forefather Moses did. He rather suffer affliction with his people. “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter”: he refused to follow their customs.

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God”: he chose that rather than to have riches with the other nation, “than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. Pleasure don’t last but for a season.

“Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.” Christ is the greater riches, so we got to bear our foundation on Jesus the Christ. The sin is just for a season; sin equals death, but the gift of God is eternal life. So we got to put our faith on Jesus Christ.

precepts.why: “For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” That’s the only foundation. The Most High God knew that, so in order for us to be delivered, in order for our sins to be wiped away, we had to be groomed and prepared to receive Christ.

sense.text: “Rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, as other people: for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God”. That was prophesied: because you wanted to do that, he’s going to turn his face away from us. “Thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor”: that’s going into sin, into the idolatry, the fornication. We loved that rather than the laws of God.

“I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time”: at the beginning, at the first time, we were supposed to be great, supposed to be righteous. “But they went to Baal–peor”: we decided to serve the devil.

“And separated themselves unto that shame”: that shame is that nakedness, that sin. “And their abominations were according as they loved”: that’s going into the idols and their lust.

precepts.why: “But while men slept”: when we slept, when we sinned, “his enemy came”. The enemy is the devil. We did this to ourselves, brothers and sisters. The fathers found as the firstripe at the first time went to Baal-peor; while we slept in sin, the enemy came and sowed his tares.

Their abominations were according as they loved. “And she hath changed my judgments into wickedness more than the nations”: God gave us the law, the commandments, the judgments, and we changed it into wickedness, more than the other nations. You ever seen an Edomite homosexual? You’re like, yeah, he’s gay or whatever. But when you see a Jake homosexual, oh my gosh. When you go to some of these places, it’s outright ridiculous. We take sin to the utmost extreme. What are we reading in the Bible? It shows just that: we are the people, in our greatness and in our folly.

“And my statutes more than the countries that are round about her: for they have refused my judgments and my statutes, they have not walked in them.” God did everything for us, but that’s what happens when you spoil somebody. When you spoil a child, are they ever grateful? No. That’s Israel: we are that spoiled child. We had everything handed to us and we forsook our father.

sense.text: “I remember thee, the kindness of thy youth, the love of thine espousals, when thou wentest after me in the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.” I remember thee at the first, the kindness of thy youth.

“Israel was holiness unto the Lord”: there was a point where we was getting it right; we was holiness unto the Lord. “And the firstfruits of his increase: all that devour him shall offend; evil shall come upon them, saith the Lord.” He protected us; he was that hedge. Anybody mess with us, he would destroy the nations. How can one chase a thousand except the Lord be with him? Our rock is not like their rock. That’s how it was when we was holy.

“Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods?” When it comes to all the other nations, they still got their wicked gods; they don’t change their gods. They stay true to their idols, which are no gods. But we, who have the one true God, turn to these idols. “But my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.”

“Be astonished, O ye heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid, be ye very desolate, saith the Lord. For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.” Idols can’t hold no truth; they are teachers of lies. We gave up the living water, the fountain of life, for cisterns that can’t hold no truth.

“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine”: he planted us a noble vine, to be fruitful, to be that grape, “wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” He don’t even recognize us: who are these people? I didn’t create them like this.

That’s like the worst thing, to be a father and raise your son up in his truth and then he bugs the hell out; or God forbid you have a daughter who you keep close to you and she goes and plays the harlot. That’s how the Most High God felt about us. It hurts worse with the daughter, and that’s why we’re referred to as the woman. When it’s your daughter or your wife, and it said espousals earlier, just think about her getting dogged out: that make you want to do something. That’s why the Most High said, I walk away from y’all before I destroy you off the face of the earth. Remember, Moses had to remind the Most High, hey, you made a covenant; he was about to do it.

Technically we don’t deserve no forgiveness for what we did. You gonna forgive your wife if she get dogged out? But the Most High loves us so much he gonna give us mercy.

Degenerate means having declined or become less specialized in nature, character, structure or function from an ancestral or former state. Remember, we was holy; then we became unholy. It also means having sunk to a condition below that which is normal to a type, like fruit so degenerate that the insects weren’t even interested. That’s Israel right there: a fruit so degenerate that the insects don’t even want to feed off of it. Remember Isaiah 5:6: he wouldn’t prune us; he’d leave it unkept to the point where we were withered away.

“So thou, O son of man, I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; therefore thou shalt hear the word at my mouth, and warn them from me.” If the watchman does not warn the wicked, “that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.” But if he warns him and “he do not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul.” As a watchman, you’ve done your job. If they don’t want to listen, if they don’t want to hearken, it is what it is.

“If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live?” To pine is to lose vigor, health or flesh. That’s what we did: we lost our boldness, we lost our integrity, we lost all of that to the point where we were withered away. We were degenerate.

How should we then live? What’s our only option, brothers and sisters? Christ. That’s the only way. If we didn’t have Christ, we would all have died off.

precepts.why:
The answer to how should we then live: “Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby ye have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die, O house of Israel?” The Most High is asking: I gave y’all everything; y’all bring this upon yourself. You’re suffering because of your own sin. Why would you die, Israel? Why would you continue to be degenerate and pine away?

“For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth”: that’s the merciful one, being merciful to his inheritance. He has no pleasure in you dying in your sins. “Wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.” So, Israel, let’s turn away from these sins, these idols, and let’s live unto the Most High in Christ.

sense.text: Our only hope in the world is through Christ. These other camps out here say only the Most High: there’s no salvation for you, idiot. But if you want to repent from your wicked ways and receive Christ, you have a chance. “Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the Lord hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.”

“But Zion said, The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me.” That’s basically saying, I ain’t got no hope; I’ve seen so much, I ain’t got hope. You may have felt like that before, but we got Christ.

precepts.why: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins”. This man is Jesus the Christ. “And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” There it is: we have that chance at salvation, that mercy and forgiveness. Zion is not forgotten.

Zion said the Lord hath forsaken me. “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” God has not cast away his people.

sense.text: “For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God”: both southern and northern kingdom. The prophecy in Ezekiel 37 is being fulfilled, not just the circumcision but the uncircumcision as well.

“But ye have received the Spirit of adoption”: we read that earlier in Ephesians 1:5, how we were chosen before the foundation of the world and predestined for this adoption. “Whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”.

“And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”: we are up next, the lineage, the children behind the Most High in Christ. “If so be that we suffer with him”. We’re not going to make it out of this without going through what we deserve. Just because he’s going to forgive us doesn’t mean he just forgot about it. A lot of brothers and sisters come into this truth and say this is the greatest thing. It is the greatest thing, but you better know what you signed up for. You are going to go through it; there ain’t no escaping that.

Christ ain’t did no sin, and didn’t he have to suffer for what we did? So why do you think we exempt? Are we greater than Christ? Absolutely not. He was glorified, and if we want to be glorified we got to do the same exact thing. Think about all the sin you did: you deserve to go through it; Christ did not. But he loves us so much he said, I’m going to take this L for you. Sometimes we do any and everything to try to avoid facing the affliction that we deserve; we have to change our minds. “That we may be also glorified together”: that’s what we want, that reward, that consolation, that prize, but we got to get ready to suffer.

“For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.” We read that like it’s words on paper, but none of us can fully understand it. We don’t see it like that because we don’t see heavenly things, we don’t see how the Most High sees it. That’s why we have to read the scriptures, meditate on it, and pray for the Most High to build up our spirits, so when it does come we can go through with it.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” That’s going into the creation. “For the creature was made subject to vanity”: how was that? When we went into idolatry. “Not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope”.

“Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.” The trees, the birds, the animals, the whole creation groaneth, because they hate the way that they’re being treated. There are destroyers of the earth, like when you read Revelation 11:18. The ruling power on the earth right now is not treating and governing the earth correctly, so the creation is groaning. They can’t wait for the rightful possessors of this world to come back into rulership.

“And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit”: that’s our rightful, original state. We were made to be holy. That’s why oppression maketh a wise man mad: he’s the way that God created him to be, holy. “Even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.”

“For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope”. “But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.” What is that hope? That faith: Jesus Christ. That’s the only hope in the world that we got.

“Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” That’s the holy spirit bringing all things to our memories. When we pray, Christ is the intercessor, the in-between: he takes the right things up to the Most High. A lot of times you say a lot of nonsense and he’s like, nope, not taking that; I’ma take what needs to be done to the Most High. That’s why the Most High allowed this to happen: because we need Christ, because we ain’t right.

“And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.” So when we say it wrong, he lines it up according to the will of God so it can be answered.

“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose”: according to his purpose that was predestined for this. “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. It ain’t for everybody; it ain’t for all Israel. We already established that a lot of our people ain’t going to receive it. “That he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

“Whom he called, them he also justified”: justified from all things, from all sins. Now we have a chance through Christ Jesus. “And whom he justified, them he also glorified”: the sins will be wiped away. But don’t forget, we ain’t getting past the tribulation. We cannot skip the tribulation. That’s the Christianity mindset: oh, I repented, all things are good in the blood of Jesus, I’m going to heaven. No. What about all that stuff you did? What about what Christ had to suffer? Are you better? Absolutely not. It don’t work like that.

“If God be for us, who can be against us? He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all”: he didn’t even spare his own Son. That shows how much he loved us. We’re not worthy of his Son, but he delivered him up for us. “How shall he not with him also freely give us all things? Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God’s elect? It is God that justifieth. Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.”

This clarifies that mindset of just repenting and then being glorified. “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?” In these last days, our family members are going to try to separate us from the love of God. When you read this, don’t read it the same no more. People say, oh, I didn’t make the sabbath today, who shall separate us. No, it’s much more than that. “Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?” That’s what it’s really talking about: life or death, torture; famine, not eating; nakedness, not having clothes; peril, troublesome times; sword, guns. This is real.

“As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long”. That does not mean something else; that’s what it means. We are killed all the day long, for Christ. “We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” That’s showing you how it’s going to be as we get closer to harvest.

precepts.why: The creature was made subject to vanity when we went into idolatry. “Be not wroth with us, but spare thy people, and have mercy upon thine own inheritance: for thou art merciful unto thy creature.” Thou art merciful unto thy creature: the creature subjected to vanity is subjected in hope of that mercy.

This shows why the creation can’t wait: because of the destroyers of the earth. “When thou shalt besiege a city a long time, in making war against it to take it, thou shalt not destroy the trees thereof by forcing an axe against them: for thou mayest eat of them, and thou shalt not cut them down (for the tree of the field is man’s life)”. Does Esau listen to that? No. All he does is destroy, destroy, destroy. That’s why the creation is groaning: they want us to come back, because we would apply that law.

Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? “Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee”. They’re going to try to discredit this truth, to make you not believe, to weaken your faith. That’s one thing.

What else will try to separate us? “For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Persecution against those who fear the Lord. That is the tribulation, distress and persecution of Romans 8:35: it’s much more than missing a sabbath.

sense.text:
It is not to scare anybody, but it has to be gone over: see what the Most High calls it. “For our light affliction”. He calls it light, because the kingdom is so great that we cannot even imagine what is coming. All the tribulation, persecution, famine and sword is “but for a moment”, only for a moment.

That light affliction “worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.” If we want that glorified state, that glorification, we have to go through this light affliction. People say, man, how are you calling that light? It is the Messiah, and we are not going to understand his ways. He is telling us: you think that is bad, but that is how great it is going to be in the kingdom.

“While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal”. This ain’t real. Outside the matrix, anything that don’t last forever ain’t real. The monetary system ain’t real. Your job ain’t real, because they can fire you tomorrow, and if you get sick and die, won’t they replace you the next day?

The only thing that is real and has substance is something that can last forever: “the things which are not seen are eternal.” That is what we have to strive for. We have to change the way that we think.

“And the times of this ignorance God winked at”. God winked at our ignorance. So let all of that degenerate stuff go: all of the acting a fool, chasing divers lusts. Let that thing go.

“But now commandeth all men every where to repent”. Now he commands us all to repent and follow Christ. This is where the class really begins: the harvest is coming, and the only way to be ready for it is true repentance.

precepts.why:
“I acknowledged my sin unto thee”: that is what we have to do. That is the first step in repentance, acknowledging it and making supplication. “And mine iniquity have I not hid”: you have to come clean with that thing.

“I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin.” So if we want to be forgiven, if we want to be justified, we have to confess our sins. That is how the command to repent is answered.

“Yet they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.” This is what we do not want to repeat. We come into this truth and then take it for granted. We go through the motions in this truth when God has given us a second chance unto Christ. We hit and miss on the Sabbath, and we treat our brothers and sisters any type of way.

No, Israel, we are not to be like that, not to be like our forefathers. That is how you harden your neck: acting like this thing ain’t the most important thing in your life. It should be what you think about on the daily. The scripture should be flowing daily, and we should be trying to be here every day if we can.

When we were in wickedness, we took it to a whole other level. So we have to do the same thing coming back to Christ in our repentance.

This is the mindset we have to be in. We ain’t going to get the kingdom just by thinking we repented and God is going to bless us and it is all over. No, we have to actually put in some work.

“For as it was your mind to go astray from God”: that is what we did, we went astray, and we are still going astray to this day. People make excuses to miss the Sabbath, and make excuses to sin as if it is a light thing. It is not a light thing when you decide to sin.

“So, being returned, seek him ten times more.” Think about how wicked you were in the world: how you never missed the club, never missed the opportunity to celebrate Christmas. You put so much effort into doing those sins to the top of your abilities. Do the same thing in God ten times more. We have to put forth that much effort into coming back to being righteous and keeping God’s commandments.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” We have to do any and everything in our power to keep ourselves from our iniquity. We have to stay busy. Think: what else can I do for this truth? How can I put my brick in? How can I keep from being idle?

Always keep this at the forefront: “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.”

Whatever we have done, it is not forgotten. We may have forgotten it, but the Most High God has made a record of that thing. “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are made manifest unto God”.

“Therefore all their works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon their ways.” The Most High sees everything. All of our works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon our ways.

“None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him”. So we have to find a way to stop sinning, because he sees it all, and all of it is being documented. The harvest is coming, brothers and sisters, whether we want to believe it or not: “all their sins are before the Lord”.

“But the Lord being gracious, and knowing his workmanship, neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.” He spared us and has given us a chance to get it right. That is the command to repent: a chance to get it right.

“He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.” Everything that we think is hid will be brought forth to light, in this earth or in judgment.

So going through these precepts, we have to change our mindset and realize how good a spot we are really in: to be here today knowing who you are, knowing that Christ is black, that the angels are black, and that Christ came for you.

sense.text: “For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline”. Knowing that the Most High sees everything, we have to desire discipline, meaning we have to desire the laws of God, the discipline of the Most High God. “And the care of discipline is love”.
“And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed unto her laws is the assurance of incorruption”.

“And incorruption maketh us near unto God”. So we cannot go back to what our forefathers were doing, being that degenerate plant, that wild grape. We have to be incorruptible, meaning we have to be keeping the laws of God.

precepts.why:
In these times the only thing that is going to keep us is this Bible. “And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.”

In these perilous times the only thing that will keep us going is wisdom and knowledge. Think about The Book of Eli, with Denzel: he was blind, and all around was chaos, the way 2 Esdras 16 talks about the people that are left and everything being scarce. But he was maintained and he was good because he had the Bible, the last Bible at that time in that movie. That is the discipline we have to desire.

sense.text:
“As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten”. You are not just going to make it to the kingdom scot-free. The Most High loves Israel, and those who diligently seek him. When you make your mistakes, because he loves you he is going to chasten you so you can get it right, because he is going to have mercy on you. But mercy ain’t the same for everybody, so don’t take advantage of it.

“Be zealous therefore, and repent”. When you get jacked up and chased, you have to be zealous and desire the discipline. You should be spiritual enough, when certain things go bad in your life, to say: okay, I know why that happened, I wasn’t doing right right here, and the Most High spared me and made it come out a different way. It’s crazy how some people, when they did wrong, want to argue. Bro, the Most High is sparing you. You may be getting chastened, but you deserve death; he is just sparing you right now for some folly you did. You have to be spiritual enough to see that thing.

“Behold, I stand at the door, and knock”: Christ is standing at the door for us. “If any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.” We have a chance to repent, a chance at forgiveness and salvation, and it is given to us by Christ. All we have to do is answer the call, and desire discipline, desire that knowledge and that wisdom.

“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne”. It does not say it to everybody, not to everybody that comes in here and sits down. It is to him that overcomes all those trials, tribulations and persecutions, who will sit with him in his throne in the kingdom.

“Even as I also overcame”. He overcame, so we have to do the same thing. He was sent for our example, because before Christ we were not doing it right, so the Most High sent Christ for our example. “And am set down with my Father in his throne.”

Now we get the understanding of the whole parable and tie this thing together. “He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man”: that is the same one knocking at the door. The one that sowed the good seed is Christ.

“The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom”. Remember we are supposed to be those grapes, those noble vines. The good seed is us, the children of Israel.

“But the tares are the children of the wicked one”: the wicked of our people and the other nations.

“The enemy that sowed them is the devil”. We got caught up with the devil when we fell into sin.

“The harvest is the end of the world”. Wait a second: the harvest is the end of the world. So now the class is talking about the end of the world. “And the reapers are the angels.”

“As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world.” Just like the tares are going to be destroyed in the fire, that is how it is going to be in the end of the world.

“The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity”. Everything that does sin is going to be destroyed off the face of the earth.
“And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.”

“Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun”, spelled s-u-n, “in the kingdom of their Father.” We are going to be heirs with Christ, and we are going to shine as the sun. “Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.”

precepts.why:
2 Esdras 6 says that the harvest is the end of the world. “Whosoever remaineth from all these that I have told thee shall escape”: all these things are the persecutions, the famine, the pestilence. Whoever remains from all these things shall “see my salvation, and the end of your world.”

That is harvest time. He gave us all this time to get it right, because remember, we were degenerate. We pined away, we became nothing, the lowest of the low. But he gave us all this time to get it right, and now he is coming to reap his crop.

“And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth: and the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.”

This shows what “turned into another meaning” is going into. “In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.”

Those who see the end of the world, the salvation and the destruction, shall be changed. “For this corruptible must put on incorruption”: this sinful body, the sinful flesh, must put on incorruptible flesh. Our bodies have to be changed at the harvest.

The reapers are the angels. “And another angel came out from the altar, which had power over fire; and cried with a loud cry to him that had the sharp sickle”: remember, the angels are the reapers.

“Thrust in thy sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth; for her grapes are fully ripe.” Now they are fully ripe. They were not ripe before; they were wild grapes, and they had to get their mind right so they could receive Christ.

“And the angel thrust in his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.” That is going into the wicked of our people, and most importantly into the nations.

“But the day of doom shall be the end of this time”. That is the day of doom: World War III, those nuclear missiles. That is the being destroyed with fire.

“And the beginning of the immortality for to come”: changed into another meaning, like 2 Esdras 6 says. These bodies ain’t immortal, so a change has to take place. “Wherein corruption is past”: the sin is past. That is what it is talking about.

This is what corruption being past means: “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”. That is tangible, something real. When corruption passes, the children of Israel shall all be righteous, and that is going to be permanent.

“My right hand shall not spare the sinners”: his hand is not going to spare the sinners. “And my sword shall not cease over them that shed innocent blood upon the earth.”

“The fire is gone forth from his wrath, and hath consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners, like the straw that is kindled.” Those are the tares right there; they are going to be destroyed.

“Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.” Destruction to them that sin. “I will not spare them: go your way, ye children, from the power, defile not my sanctuary.”

“For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”. That parallels the furnace of fire perfectly. “And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: all that do wickedly shall be put to death. “And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.”

“But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings”, Sun spelled s-u-n. That is going into Christ. We are going to be heirs with Christ, and we are going to shine as the sun. “And ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.”

“And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the Lord of hosts.”

Now see what is going to happen to the tares, the ones on the other end. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours. When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.”

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach”. These are the ones who put the incredulity on us, who tried to weaken our faith, who persecuted us and spoke evil of us, the chosen.

“We fools accounted his life madness”. “How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!” All of our enemies are going to witness that we are the children of God. That is a heavy thing, brothers and sisters.

“And the light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us.” The Sun of righteousness is going to shine upon those who fear the Lord, and they will be with him. Those it never rose upon are the ones getting burnt up.

sense.text:
“Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. The wicked of our people are going to be destroyed, and this place that we are in right now will also be destroyed.

“Saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob”: he is going to spare some. He ain’t going to destroy all of us.
“For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.”

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword”: again, the wicked of our people are going to die by the sword. “Which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us”. That is the people. It is like the movie the Bishop recommended, American Refugee: they didn’t prepare because they didn’t think it could actually happen, and then they were at the discretion of their white neighbor. The white neighbor took the man’s wife, because he didn’t believe the evil could touch him.

“In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. For those who are going to repent, those who are going to be appreciative of the mercy, the Most High God said he is going to flip things around for us.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom”: role reversal. “And of all the heathen, which are called by my name”: Christians, fake Jews. That is what it is talking about, all the heathen that are called by his name.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt.” All the hills are going to be destroyed: that melting is destruction.

“And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof”.

“And they shall no more be pulled up out of their land”. No more Assyrians, no more Amalek stealing our land. We are going to occupy our land forever, in that day when the harvest comes.

precepts.why: He ain’t going to destroy all of us. “Thus saith the Lord, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it”. The blessing in the cluster is those who fear the Lord. That is the saving of the house of Jacob in Amos 9:8.

These are the ones that say the evil shall not overtake them. “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement”. That is our people that trust in America. You would think it is only talking about our family members that are not in this truth, but many of y’all in this truth trust in America’s system. Many of y’all put your jobs above the work of the Most High. A lot of y’all cannot fathom America falling; you can’t see it. You are at agreement with hell and death.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through”: that is the evil that is going to come. “It shall not come unto us”: that is what our people truly believe. They think that even when it does hit the fan, they are going to be good.

“For we have made lies our refuge”. This kingdom is not forever. It is a lie, it is temporal, but the kingdom of heaven is forever.

sense.text:
“Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest, and thy pride unto the Mighty.” Deacon Isaac touched on it a few nights ago: that prideful dealing, going into space and fornicating. They are getting bolder and bolder with this transgender LG, whatever it is.

The article: a transgender man who gave birth to his son criticized his medical staff for calling him mother, and claims it is important to stop automatically linking pregnancy with being a woman. Do y’all see this foolishness? This is straight confusion, the land of confusion. They are the destroyers of the earth, not just physically: they are changing everything upside down.

precepts.why:
“Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin”.

“That walk to go down into Egypt”: we did it, our forefathers did it before, and guess what, we are doing the same thing. This is spiritual Egypt right here. “To strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt”: making the covenant with hell and death.

“Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.” Your confusion, because now they are trying to say that women are not the only people that can give birth. That is why we have to have the Bible. This is going to be our stability in these last days.

“I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.” Bear children. God says that the women bear children. We don’t give a damn what Esau is saying.

The land of confusion. “Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter’s clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?”

The things they have turned upside down, now saying that pregnancy and birth are not just for a woman: God is about to put all of that to rest. The harvest is coming.

There is some wicked stuff right here. “When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice”. When the righteous are in authority they are going to bring the laws of the Most High God and set everything in order, and the people will rejoice, because we are following Christ and we are going to set the order right.

“But when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.” There is mourning stuff right here. With the wicked in rulership of this world right now, you see stuff like this happening. This is not the laws of the Most High God; this is not right. But God is going to turn that thing around, and it is coming.

sense.text: “And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins”.
“For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.”

“Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works: in the cup which she hath filled fill to her double.” It is going to be role reversal. But Israel, we cannot get caught up in America’s faults. We have to take advantage of the mercy that the Most High God gave his people.

precepts.why:
“Behold, saith God, I will call together all the kings of the earth to reverence me, which are from the rising of the sun”: that is the Far East. “From the south, from the east, and Libanus; to turn themselves one against another, and repay the things that they have done to them”: repay what they did to God’s people.

As the harvest gets closer, this is what you see; we are approaching it. The article: a general saying a major conflict between great powers is more likely, that we are now facing two global powers, China and Russia, with significant military capabilities, both intending to fundamentally change the rules-based global order, and that the potential for significant international conflict is increasing, not decreasing. We are getting closer to the harvest, brothers and sisters. Understand that thing.

“Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth”. Remember that wisdom and knowledge will be the stability in these times; we have to stay in the Bible. “And keepeth his garments”: keep our garments clean and spotless, a representation of resisting sin, “lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.”

“And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon.” That is 2 Esdras 15:20. We are seeing World War III being developed right before our eyes.

“And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done.” Voices, thunders, lightnings, and “a great earthquake, such as was not since men were upon the earth”.

“And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell”. That is talking about America. The city of the nations is the great melting pot: America has all nations, kindreds and tongues here. So while World War III is being developed, America is going to fall.

“And great Babylon came in remembrance before God”. We may have forgotten; we may think God don’t see. But no, Babylon, America, will be remembered by the Most High God, the way he hath remembered her iniquities, and when it is harvest, whoever ain’t doing right is going to be burnt up with America, “to give unto her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath.”

sense.text:
What do we have to do to survive? “The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites.” The sinners of our people are the ones who are going to be afraid.

“Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?” Who is going to survive all this fire and burning?

“He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions”: stealing, dealing falsely, filthy lucre. Don’t get caught up in these things. Sin sticks close to buying and selling; don’t get caught up in foolishness in these last days just to earn a few dollars.

“That shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil”: those who keep themselves from their iniquity.

precepts.why:
“Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the Lord hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.”

“But Zion said, The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me.” That is the sinful of our people, the sinners in Zion who are going to be afraid.

“So shall righteousness hate iniquity”. That is how we are going to survive in these last days: we must hate iniquity.

“When she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” Nothing is hid. Christ is coming back to defend us, and he has been watching the whole time, so you can’t fake the funk. He is only coming back to deliver those he searched diligently and saw keeping the commandments and being righteous in these last days.

sense.text: This goes along with the teaching: it shows those that are going to be delivered, that God will preserve, and those that were made for judgment. “All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.”

“There be spirits that are created for vengeance”. There are spirits all around about us made for vengeance on those that torment this earth and torment the children of Israel, “which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.” That is God: God created those forces to destroy those that have tormented this earth.

“Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance”. That is the fire you hear about going all around in California, the tornadoes, the earthquakes, the floods, the famine you see going on today.

“Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword, punishing the wicked to destruction.” The wicked are those of our people and the other nations that are not keeping God’s laws. They will be punished.
“They shall rejoice in his commandment”. They will do gladly what God created them to do. That goes along with the missiles that are going to be coming and destroying this place.
Going into the harvest. “Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off.” All the enemies of the Most High’s people shall be cut off.
“I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots”: tanks and all of that stuff. All of their weapons of war are going to be destroyed.
“And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds”. “And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers”.

“Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands.” No more idols: no more Hindu, no more Islam, no more white Jesus. It is going to be destroyed when the harvest comes.

“And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities.”

“And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard.” Such as they have never heard before.

precepts.why:
What he did to the Egyptians, everybody heard that; it was a big thing on the earth. But he is saying this destruction that is coming to the heathen, this ass whooping, nobody has ever heard the like of before.

“I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.” “For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.”

“And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man”. Even at that time the nations didn’t want to mess with us, “because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.”

sense.text:
“For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; The daughter of Babylon is like a threshingfloor, it is time to thresh her”. It is getting close.

“Yet a little while, and the time of her harvest shall come.” The time of harvest will come, brothers and sisters. We just have to be patient.

“Because of the wrath of the Lord it shall not be inhabited, but it shall be wholly desolate”. “All ye that bend the bow, shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she hath sinned against the Lord.” He has remembered Babylon’s iniquity, and he is saying to all the nations: fire off those missiles at Babylon.
“Her foundations are fallen, her walls are thrown down: for it is the vengeance of the Lord: take vengeance upon her; as she hath done, do unto her.”

“Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him that handleth the sickle in the time of harvest: for fear of the oppressing sword they shall turn every one to his people, and they shall flee every one to his own land.”

“And I will bring Israel again to his habitation”. While this is going on, the harvest is going into their destruction and our salvation. Their destruction, and the destruction of the wicked of our people, is going to be our salvation in the time of harvest. “And he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.”

“The iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found”, because we will all be righteous in that day.

“For I will pardon them whom I reserve.” He reserved us; he preserved us from the beginning. We have to be patient, and most importantly we have to be thankful for the mercy that the Most High is showing us.

We are all familiar with Joel 3, how it goes into Tyre and Zidon selling us to the Grecians. “Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head”. The Most High is going to repay them double, like we read earlier.

“And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah”: we just read that in Amos as well. “And they shall sell them to the Sabeans”: that is the Cushites, “to a people far off: for the Lord hath spoken it.” In that day certain nations are going to have a different hierarchy.

“Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near”. “Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.” “Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat”. All roads lead to World War III in the day of harvest: “for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.”

“Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe”: the harvest is ripe at this time. “For the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.” It is going to get to the point where the Most High just can’t take it no more, and he has to send Christ to reap.
“Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.” The valley of decision is Megiddo, Armageddon.

“The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining.” “The Lord also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake”.

“But the Lord will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.” When their destruction comes, the Lord will be the hope of his people. So, brothers and sisters, don’t play yourself. Be patient, and let this thing play out.
“So shall ye know that I am the Lord your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more.”
“Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.”

“But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.” That is a beautiful thing right there. “For I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed: for the Lord dwelleth in Zion.”

precepts.why: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemy come together: that is the Lord being the hope of his people while the heavens and the earth shake. All praise to the Most High God.

sense.text: Wrapping up. “Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power.”
“For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet.” Christ must reign till he has put all enemies under his feet, and then he is going to give all power and dominion to the Father.

precepts.why: “And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him”. No more slavery, no more oppression. The curse is finally going to be broken in the day of harvest, brothers and sisters.

“And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.” “In righteousness shalt thou be established”: the world is going to be established in righteousness for once.

“Thou shalt be far from oppression”, because the curse is no more; it is going to be gone. “For thou shalt not fear: and from terror; for it shall not come near thee.”

Why is that? “And it shall come to pass, when ye be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days, saith the Lord, they shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of the Lord: neither shall it come to mind”.

“At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord”: in that time all the world shall call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord. “And all the nations shall be gathered unto it, to the name of the Lord, to Jerusalem: neither shall they walk any more after the imagination of their evil heart.” Jerusalem is going to be the world’s capital on the earth.

The last scripture. “For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him.” Keep this at the forefront and realize that what is waiting for us is far better than the oppression and the tribulation we are going to have to go through.
